How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide for building a **RESTful GET** request to the *“Get information of device connector versions”* API in Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1. It covers the UI steps (API Explorer), the raw HTTP call, and a ready‑to‑run `curl` example. --- ## 1. Where to find the API in the Dashboard UI | Step | Action | |------|--------| | 1 | Log in to the Nexus Dashboard web console. | | 2 | From the left‑hand menu, choose **Developer Tools → API Explorer** (or **API** → **Explorer** depending on your UI layout). | | 3 | In the search box type **“device connector versions”** or the exact API name you mentioned. | | 4 | Click the matching entry – you’ll see the endpoint, HTTP method, required headers, and any query parameters. | | 5 | Click **“Generate Request”**. The UI will display the full request (URL, headers, body). | | 6 | Copy the request details or click **“Copy to Clipboard”**. | > **Tip:** The API Explorer automatically injects your current session’s bearer token into the `Authorization` header, so you don’t have to manually add it. --- ## 2. Typical request structure | Element | Example | |---------|---------| | **Base URL** | `https:///api/v1` | | **Endpoint** | `/device-connector-versions` | | **Method** | `GET` | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json` | | **Query Parameters** | Optional – e.g. `deviceId`, `connectorId`, `status`, `version` | > **Full URL (no query params):** > `https:///api/v1/device-connector-versions` > **Full URL (with a device filter):** > `https:///api/v1/device-connector-versions?deviceId=12345` --- ## 3. Example `curl` command ```bash # Replace placeholders with real values DASHBOARD_HOST="nexus-dashboard.example.com" TOKEN="eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..." curl -X GET \ "https://${DASHBOARD_HOST}/api/v1/device-connector-versions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` ### With a device filter ```bash curl -X GET \ "https://${DASHBOARD_HOST}/api/v1/device-connector-versions?deviceId=12345" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` --- ## 4. Common query parameters (if supported) | Parameter | Purpose | Example | |-----------|---------|---------| | `deviceId` | Return connector versions for a specific device | `?deviceId=12345` | | `connectorId` | Return a single connector’s version info | `?connectorId=67890` | | `status` | Filter by connector status (`active`, `inactive`, etc.) | `?status=active` | | `version` | Filter by firmware/software version | `?version=5.2.1` | | `vendor` | Filter by connector vendor | `?vendor=Cisco` | > **Note:** The exact set of supported query parameters is shown in the API Explorer. If you’re unsure, start with the base URL and add one parameter at a time. --- ## 5. Authentication & Permissions | Item | Requirement | |------|-------------| | **Bearer Token** | Must be obtained via the Dashboard’s OAuth or session login flow. | | **User Role** | The user must have at least *Read* permission on the *Device Connector* resource. | | **HTTPS** | All API calls must use HTTPS; the Dashboard does not support plain HTTP. | --- ## 6. Troubleshooting | Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix | |---------|--------------|-----| | `401 Unauthorized` | Token expired or missing | Refresh the token or re‑authenticate | | `403 Forbidden` | Insufficient permissions | Verify the user role and resource ACLs | | `404 Not Found` | Wrong endpoint or host | Double‑check the base URL and endpoint path | | `400 Bad Request` | Invalid query parameter | Validate the parameter names/values against the API docs | --- ## 7. Quick sanity check After running the `curl` command, you should receive a JSON payload similar to: ```json { "total": 3, "items": [ { "connectorId": "67890", "deviceId": "12345", "vendor": "Cisco", "firmwareVersion": "5.2.1", "status": "active", "lastUpdated": "2024-05-12T08:34:00Z" }, ... ] } ``` If you see an empty `items` array, double‑check that the device/connector actually exists and that your query filters match real data. --- ### TL;DR 1. **Open API Explorer** → find “device connector versions” → click **Generate Request**. 2. Copy the URL, add your bearer token, and hit **GET**. 3. Use the provided `curl` snippet as a template. That’s all you need to pull connector‑version data from Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1. Happy querying!
